page.layout: One printed page, single column of text. Top: woodcut ornamental border (not text). Then title block centred in large type, followed by a centred paragraph of smaller type, a centred heading "LOCUS I." with a second heading "DE THEOLOGIA IN GENERE.", then numbered theses (I.–IV.) in italic with marginal references at the right end of lines, and a signature line at the foot.

main_text.head: SYLLABUS CONTROVERSIARUM PRÆCIPUARUM, Quæ, Orthodoxos inter & heterodoxos agitata, in Medulla definiuntur, & Polemicis exercitationibus argumentum suppeditant.
main_text.p: Ubi litera G. Gentiles; J. Judæos; M. Muhammedanos; Lib. Libertinos; S. Socinianos; P. Pontificios; F. Fanaticos, V Veigelianos, Enthusiastas; A. Anabaptistas; C. Pseudo-criticos; Pol-Pseudo-politicos; Gr. Græcos; R. Remonstrantes; L. Lutheranos, quibus cum positiones controversæ sunt, signant.
main_text.head: LOCUS I. DE THEOLOGIA IN GENERE.
main_text.p: I. Post lapsum hominis datur Theologia naturalis, qua Deus, ejus potentia & Divinitas, etiam sine revelatione supernaturali, cognoscitur. S. Sect. 4.
II. Naturalis Dei cognitio sine notitia Christi non est salutaris. R. 4.
III. Non datur religio communis, solius naturæ principiis innixa & salutifera. S. R. 5. 6.
IV. Religio Gentilium, Judæorum, Muhammedanorum religionis veræ criteriis destituitur. G. J. M. 9.

page.notes: The title block is set in large roman and italic capitals and small italic type; the woodcut border above it is decorative. The final line "V. Sa-" is a catchword-like fragment at the foot right and is treated as a catchword in the text. Marginal references in the theses are printed inline at line ends. Show-through from the reverse page is visible faintly and omitted.
